root_cause.text: The `bpf_prog_verify_signature` function lacked a size limit check on `attr->signature_size`, allowing userspace to pass an arbitrarily large value that forces the kernel into expensive memory allocation paths (kmalloc_large or vmalloc), enabling potential denial-of-service abuse.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (attr->signature_size > KMALLOC_MAX_CACHE_SIZE) return -EINVAL;` in `kernel/bpf/syscall.c`, and the commit message explicitly states "Allowing larger sizes opens the door for abuse by passing excessive size values and forcing the kernel into expensive allocation paths (via kmalloc_large or vmalloc)."
